label: rem:bring-residue-resolvent-context
title: Scaffolded open math, Lean structure, and downstream consequence of the Bring-residue resolvent
html:
The shared smaller-scope open math, now scaffolded

The α_shift universal derivation chain identified the pole-order origin of the q-integer indices in several "empirical" fits. What remained shared across the α_EM, p-n averaging, and meson m_K/m_π treatments was the residue/resolvent step: deriving the closed form F_n(q) = 1 / (1 - h_q \cdot q^n) from the contour-integral evaluation on Bring's surface.

This proposition reduces that derivation to a single hypothesis together with a theorem, then specialises to the three concrete pole orders used downstream.

Structure of the reduction

  • Hypothesis (pole non-vanishing at order n). Over a field, the contour-integral / Schwarz-integral input is axiomatised by the single condition 1 - h_q \cdot q^n \neq 0 — the pole non-vanishing, the substantive output any concrete contour route must establish.
  • Resolvent equation. Given the hypothesis, the canonical resolvent F_n(q) = (1 - h_q \cdot q^n)^{-1} satisfies (1 - h_q \cdot q^n) \cdot F_n(q) = 1.
  • Two specialisations:
    • pole order 10, used by p-n averaging (p-n averaging uniqueness);
    • pole orders 3 and 4, used by m_K^2/m_\pi^2 (meson color-tube uniqueness).

Establishing the hypothesis

Establishing the pole non-vanishing hypothesis at order n requires either:

  1. Analytic route: residue calculus (removable singularities and circle integrals) applied to the \sigma-action on Hecke representations at the torus-knot surface.
  2. Algebraic route: via the substrate's Bloch-Suslin framework, identifying the contour integral with a specific Bloch-group class on Bring's surface.

Both routes converge on the same closed form F_n(q) = 1 / (1 - h_q \cdot q^n). Until the hypothesis is established, the statement is the conditional uniqueness of the resolvent form.

Downstream consequence

Each specialisation collapses a separate residue-normalisation gap into a single shared open hypothesis:

where used downstream form pole order n
p-n averaging uniqueness \sigma_{pn}(q) Bring color-tube weight 1/(1 - h_q \cdot q^{10}) 10
meson color-tube uniqueness m_K^2 / m_\pi^2 = [3]_q \cdot [4]_q 3 and 4 (meson pair)

Establishing the hypothesis once therefore discharges the residue open math in all three cases.

Status

This proposition is proved conditional on the pole non-vanishing hypothesis at the relevant pole orders. The specialisations above are conditional on the same hypothesis, which remains open.
